key_insight: UNIEGO shows that egocentric video models can learn richer representations by using multiple proxy teachers that provide complementary knowledge from other viewpoints, modalities, and foundation models. The result is a unified representation that still works using only egocentric video at deployment time.
problem_solved: Egocentric video is limited by the narrow, single-view perspective of wearable cameras, making it hard for one model to capture the full context of human actions. This paper addresses how to build a more expressive egocentric representation without requiring extra modalities or views at inference.
method: Uses a hierarchical multi-teacher distillation framework to transfer knowledge from diverse proxy sources into one egocentric student model.
Integrates complementary supervision from different viewpoints, modalities, and foundation model representations during training.
Learns a unified representation that remains deployable from egocentric video alone.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical recipe for improving video understanding without adding deployment complexity. It is especially useful for wearable computing, action recognition, and downstream egocentric tasks where richer representations can boost performance.

paper_title: UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning
